item.content:encoded:
God, I think I commented here a couple years ago, but my mind always circles back to this article whenever I get involved with the site, and I just get more and more pissed. I'm not even changing my vote, I'm sure I gave it a +1, but whatever.

All this justification that "well TECHNICALLY we don't know what Montauk is, your MIND fills in the spookiest parts" doesn't honestly matter. With the amnestics, the "she has to be aware and we can't put her out of her misery" addition, everything, we still know it's some form of torment. Whether it's physical or psychological torture or whatever else—does that really matter? My mind barely has to fill in any blanks here. The fact that a little girl is in pain is right there on the page in black and white. Procedure 110-Montauk is "tormenting an innocent child," there's nothing to fill in.

It's edgy. It's gendered. No matter how many future changes are made it will inevitably have some rape-as-shock-horror elements because of its reputation. And all of those things combine to make it feel cheap.

I like horror. I do. I wouldn't be here otherwise. I understand that it's generally scarier to let the audience draw their own conclusions. I even like horror where horrible things happen to innocent people; "Long Dream" is one or my favorite Junji Ito stories. I think this is done well because of the way people are. But I can't help but feel this wouldn't be changed all that much if it just said "the foundation tortures a child because They Will Do Anything To Secure Contain Protect". When all the scary parts are supposed to come from "the worst thing i can possibly imagine," I can just imagine some horrible thing I read in some other story. Or read "Fear Alone" and call it a day.

item.content:encoded:
A quote by Stephen King:

“The 3 types of terror: The Gross-out: the sight of a severed head tumbling down a flight of stairs, it's when the lights go out and something green and slimy splatters against your arm. The Horror: the unnatural, spiders the size of bears, the dead waking up and walking around, it's when the lights go out and something with claws grabs you by the arm. And the last and worse one: Terror, when you come home and notice everything you own had been taken away and replaced by an exact substitute. It's when the lights go out and you feel something behind you, you hear it, you feel its breath against your ear, but when you turn around, there's nothing there…”

Personally, I would rename these revulsion, fright, and dread. Revulsion being a gut-churning feeling that something is gross and disgusting. Fright being a heart-pounding feeling that something is dangerous and threatening. Dread being a head-spinny feeling that something is wrong, and you know there's something revolting or frightening out there and you're torn between looking for it and running like hell… that looming sense of doom that keeps you up at night.

Stephen King also said that he thought dread was the toughest emotion to ilicit, so he aimed for dread whenever possible. If he couldn't get to dread, he'd go for fright, and if even fright wasn't possible, he'd at least aim for revulsion (my terminology). I've kind of taken that to heart when writing horror articles.

In my analysis, 231 front-loads hard on the revulsion, skimps a bit on the terror, and keeps the dread hidden in the page source and meta-narrative. Which I guess is a tl:dr way of saying what you did. On the other hand, I'm not sure that's necessarily a bad thing. Maybe I'll think different in a few years.

item.content:encoded:
There's so many opinions on this article spanning so many different emotions and feelings that it's basically all been said before. I know Clef and am friends with him, so I'm still gonna post my opinion on this article knowing he'd vehemently disagree with it and its premise. This might also come off as me demanding the article be "SJW", but I honestly think it's worth a retrospective look at this article.

I absolutely adore the core premise. The Foundation has to do something unthinkable or unspeakable in order to keep the world alive, prevent it from dying to a terrible, terrible fate. There's a lot wrong with the Foundation already, as a powerful organization that has to do terrible things sometimes out of necessity, but I think one article exploring it is actually a really cool move. The fact that it was explored so early on in the site's history really makes this intriguing on some level as well, and I have to applaud Clef for how he went about it.

I know this originally started out as a shock horror article that basically all but implied that a young girl has to be sexually assaulted in some way in a brutal fashion. I understand that the site used to operate and thrive on being shocking, which is why it was initially seen as a horror site and still is. Being around in 2010, I remember discussion around this article and how so many people reacted to it over the years. But I think a version of this article to not make it actually disgusting (and not in the intended way) while still keeping the horror of the original concept would be super good. Maybe even posted as an alternative version.

Clef edited the article a while back to remove nearly all the implications to 231-7 being raped, which has helped, but I think the execution of this article is still fundamentally flawed. It relies too much on the reader being grossed, rather than the reader being scared. You can be both grossed and scared (and believe that being grossed achieves the same thing as being scared), but if your article is fundamentally based on grossing the reader out, you have to be super fucking good at nailing the landing to not be unintentionally gross.

I honestly can't think of how one would go about it; that's why I'm not making a suggestion, merely offering my opinion. I think there is a balance to showing that the Foundation has to go beyond the pale in order to keep humanity safe and make it terrifying without being gross. I don't think this article should be replaced with a newer version; this is honestly so heavily referenced in so many ways that it'd be impossible to replace wholly without destroying it. But I think a version like this achieving the right balance of what to do would be very interesting. I believe Clef can write something like that, or any talented writer can.

I don't believe 2317 is what I'm describing. The whole point of that is the power of belief. The people who work on 2317 believe they are doing something to save humanity even when it's impossible, and anyone not in the know thinks they're doing something terrifying. But that's not the same thing. The theme of that article is the power of belief. It doesn't go in for the theme of "The Foundation has to do something horrifying that we don't know about for the good of mankind", it's "The Foundation has to make its researchers believe they are doing something for the good of mankind". The difference is subtle, but there definitely is one. Anyway, this is my take on 231.

SCP-231 Poem

They gather round the natal bed, the foolish and the wise. They fear the child yet to be born, whose voice shall rend the skies.
The faithful watch the forest for the coming of the King. Their lanterns bright, they wait at night for the new world he shall bring.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up his clothes by casting lots.
The King is in his courting clothes; the brides are in their beds. The unborn princes wait in sleep to raise their eager heads.
The hens were in the henhouse and seven eggs did lay, till the fox crept in by dark of night and stole the eggs away.
Her screaming cries did shake the skies, as she called out for her King.
By doctor's blade the second bade a life into the world. Untimely hewn neath a silent moon, the King's red flag unfurled.
His bride the third remained unheard, her cries for help ignored. She stopped her life with a surgeon's knife, and gave it to Our Lord.
The fourth prepares a dagger and places it at her heart. The perfect cure cannot make pure what the King has set apart.
The fifth one's crown was bearing down upon the fox's set. The den was sundered with mighty thunder, an apocalypse beget.
On the sixth's day, the walls gave way, and the oceans turned to ash. Her birth gave work, as the earth shook, underneath the King's fell lash.
The seventh bride will break the tides the moon no more will shine. There comes a day not far away she'll birth the death of time.
The doctor never tells his god which one he really seeks. Instead he hides himself away, and quietly, he weeps.
For the waywardness of the simple will kill them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.
Their god's own voice, he makes the choice, declaring with their word. "In fear and pain let her remain, lest she be like the third."
And I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste from the desert to Diblah—wherever they live. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
The doctor's gun ended his run, as he put it to his ear. As she was defiled, the pitied child, he gave it to his fear.
Then a mighty angel picked up a boulder the size of a large millstone and threw it into the sea, and said: “With such violence the great city of Babylon will be thrown down, never to be found again. The music of harpists and musicians, pipers and trumpeters, will never be heard in you again. No worker of any trade will ever be found in you again. The sound of a millstone will never be heard in you again. The light of a lamp will never shine in you again. The voice of bridegroom and bride will never be heard in you again. Your merchants were the world’s important people. By your magic spell all the nations were led astray. In her was found the blood of prophets and of God’s holy people, of all who have been slaughtered on the earth.”
Her memory a fickle thing, the strongest shall endure. When her weeping starts to waver, their drugs make her mind pure.

Luke 23:34. they gather round with leering smiles, the soulless and the dead. though her soul unwinds, the cruelest minds will keep her in her bed. the potter told his 'prentice to prepare him seven jars. six he made with grace and skill, the last his hands did mar. the King is in his courting clothes, the brides are in their beds. the unborn princes wait in sleep to raise their eager heads. the hens were in the henhouse and seven eggs did lay, till the fox crept in by dark of night and stole the eggs away. six were broken by their bindings six no more shall sing. comes the seventh full unwinding and all the bells will ring. when the first had given birth, then all the birds did sing. her screaming cries did shake the skies, as she called out for her King. by doctor's blade the second bade a life into the world. untimely hewn neath a silent moon, the King's red flag unfurled. his bride the third remained unheard, her cries for help ignored. she stopped her life with a surgeon's knife, and gave it to Our Lord. the fourth prepares a dagger and places it at her heart. the perfect cure cannot make pure what the King has set apart. the fifth one's crown was bearing down upon the fox's set. the den was sundered with mighty thunder, an apocalypse beget. on the sixth's day, the walls gave way, and the oceans turned to ash. her birth gave work, as the earth shook, underneath the King's fell lash seventh bride will break the tides the moon no more will shine. there comes a day not far away she'll birth the death of time. Don't believe it when they say they're trying to save her. Why would they bother? They've got exactly what they want exactly where they want it. the doctor never tells his god which one he really seeks. instead he hides himself away, and quietly, he weeps. Proverbs 1:32 their god's own voice, he makes the choice, declaring with their word. "in fear and pain let her remain, lest she be like the third." Ezekiel 6:14 the doctor's gun ended his run, as he put it to his ear. as she was defiled, the pitied child, he gave it to his fear. Revelation 18:21-24 her memory a fickle thing, the strongest shall endure. when her weeping starts to waver, their drugs make her mind pure.

Just enter this into the console if you're on chrome, it's more than just a poem.

jQuery('span[style*="font-size"]').css({'font-size':'100%','color':'#FF0000'})

To open the console, right click anywhere, press inspect element, then press console on the bottom. A box should be there where you can paste that in, and press enter. All the text will be full-sized and bright red.
